ai.description: This slender colubrid reaches 1 meter. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and black lateral spots. A diagnostic feature is the unique, irregular dark blotching on the venter.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Wallaceophis gujaratensis* is uniquely identified by its distinct, continuous dark vertebral stripe that runs the entire length of the body, unlike the broken patterns of similar racers.
ai.habitat: *Wallaceophis gujaratensis* inhabits the semi-arid, scrub-dominated landscapes and dry deciduous forests of Gujarat, typically found at low elevations near human-altered areas.
ai.behavior: Wallace’s Striped Snake is primarily diurnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by flattening its neck and body to mimic the appearance of a venomous keelback.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Wallaceophis gujaratensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, typically from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Wallaceophis gujaratensis* is endemic to the state of Gujarat in western India, primarily inhabiting the low-elevation plains of the Saurashtra region.
